pitch: A whole role-playing adventure across the Kingdom of Procrastia, where everything gets done... eventually.

keys.Enter: Pick up what you stand on
keys.F2: Your satchel: gold, hit points, lives

news.head: Sandbox Software Gets Around to an RPG
news.html: Fans have asked for a role-playing game since our first disk. We said we'd get around to it. Quest for the Round Tuit is that. Four towns, four dungeons, two dozen people to talk to, and coastlines that curve - in Game-Maker, which nobody told us couldn't be done until we'd done it.

news.head: A horseless carriage in Procrastia
news.html: Every kingdom needs a way to get around. Procrastia's is THE CHEZ, a horseless carriage from the far-off future of 1976 and a half, waiting in Professor Fiddlesticks' garage for something with lightning in it. Charge it and drive forty leagues of tidal mud across the Dawdle Flats; its ah-OOO-gah horn clears the crabs off the causeway. Its charge port is on the rear passenger side, as always.

news.head: Since last issue: The box art made the printer
news.html: Depth Perception's box art went to the printer on time, and you've been pulling focus ever since. The trick most of you learned the hard way: a soft, see-through block isn't there right now. The trick most of you learned on the BBS: not every mirror in the Hall of Mirrors is a wall. And yes, registered players, the cardboard glasses are in your box. No, you won't need them.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: Royal hounds
news.html: Teddy and Gwinn have royal jobs this time: they're the King's two runaway hounds, and Kennelmaster Bess would like them home. Doc Leo plays himself, as usual, and his rubber chicken finally has a name of its own. Office news: Gwinn sat on command this month. Once. Nobody had a camera, but three of us saw it.

news.head: In the workshop: Where's Gwinn?
news.html: The morning after the Big Show, Gwinn's bed is empty. That's how our next game begins: Teddy's Little Bigger Adventure. Teddy has a new trick, and for the first time in a Sandbox game you'll play as somebody else, too. Somebody big, brown and still learning to sit.

news.head: Letters: "Why ray tracing?"
news.html:
"My dad says ray tracing is for serious computers. Why is it in a game?" - A reader, by modem

The Scoop replies: Because a chrome sphere on a checkerboard is the most beautiful thing a computer can draw. Tell your dad the office 486 agrees, eventually.

items.title: Cloth Map of Procrastia
items.heading: THE KINGDOM OF PROCRASTIA
items.intro: Drawn by the Royal Cartographer, who has been meaning to finish it. Dallydale in the west, Far Putoff in the east, the Dawdle Flats between. Not to scale. Nothing in Procrastia is to scale.

marks.label: Laterburg: the King, the market, the Royal Library
Someday Harbor: the long pier, THE CHEZ
The Snooze Barrows: the first piece
Teddy's clearing in the Whistling Woods
Eventually Falls: Hattie's, Doc Leo's tent
The Putoff Mines: the third piece
King Dillydally IX on his throne
The fog bank, and the Soggy Vaults below

legend: The Dawdle Flats are not shown. They are forty leagues of mud. You aren't missing anything.

items.title: A Royal Decree
items.letterhead: BY ORDER OF HIS MAJESTY KING DILLYDALLY IX
items.to: To whomever gets around to reading this
items.body:
Be it known that the Royal Round Tuit has been stolen by one LORD DEADLINE, who was not invited.

Any subject who returns the three pieces of the Round Tuit to the Tuit Table shall receive Our gratitude, a feast, and a Royal Writ (they are free; have several).

We shall see to the matter personally as soon as We get a round tuit. Which is, you will appreciate, the difficulty.

items.title: The Royal Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Compiled by Ms. Pagely of the Royal Library, who would like her books back. Lay the red film over an answer to read it.

hints.q: Where do I go first?
hints.a: North up the road from Nowish to Laterburg. Walk into the King on his throne at the top of the Garden Court: he gives you the Royal Writ.

hints.q: How do I talk to people?
hints.a: Walk into them.

hints.q: How do I buy things?
hints.a: Walk into the counter once to pay and again to take it. No money, no sale.

hints.q: I'm out of gold.
hints.a: Foes drop gems: 5 gold each, 20 for a ruby. The dungeons have chests. The kennel and the library pay rewards.

hints.q: The door in the Snooze Barrows won't open.
hints.a: It's sealed in the King's name. Get the Royal Writ from King Dillydally first, then walk into the door.

hints.q: How do I reach the Soggy Vaults?
hints.a: Walk out along Someday Harbor's long pier to the fog bank. It only clears for the Harbor Master's foghorn, which is lying in the west room of the Snooze Barrows.

hints.q: My sword bounces off the Kraken.
hints.a: From the Vaults on, bosses are too tough for wood. Buy the steel sword from Brokk in Laterburg's market for 80 gold.

hints.q: How do I get across to Far Putoff?
hints.a: In THE CHEZ. The second piece of the Tuit is full of lightning: carry it to Professor Fiddlesticks' garage in Someday Harbor and walk into the garage door.

hints.q: The bridge on the Flats is under water!
hints.a: It's the tide. Wait a few seconds and it drains again.

hints.q: The Putoff Mines' door won't let me in.
hints.a: It wants a lamp: 40 gold at Hattie's stall in Eventually Falls.

hints.q: Lord Deadline jumped out of his armor!
hints.a: That's his second act. He backs off, then charges straight at you. Face him and swing as he comes, then step aside. Six blows; he leaves a heart.

hints.q: Where is Deadline Keep's door?
hints.a: On the south side of the Keep. The road from Eventually Falls goes round the east side of the Gloomwood to it.

hints.q: The Keep's sockets won't open.
hints.a: Each one wants its piece of the Tuit. If one stays shut, you're missing that piece: the Tuit Table in the Garden Court lights a pedestal for each piece you carry.

hints.q: Where are the royal hounds?
hints.a: Teddy is in a clearing in the Whistling Woods: take the trail east off the north road. Gwinn is digging on the beach south of Someday Harbor. Walk into each, then walk into the kennel gate in the Garden Court.

hints.q: Where is the Tome of Tomorrow?
hints.a: In the Putoff Mines' old workings, west of the great gallery. Take it to the rope at the Royal Library's door.

hints.q: Where is Sir Reginald Cluckington III?
hints.a: In a glade in the Gloomwood, east of the road to Deadline Keep. Walk into him, then into the flap of Doc Leo's tent in Eventually Falls.

hints.q: What does the kazoo do?
hints.a: Press Z. A note flies straight ahead and beats nearly anything, bosses included. Lyra sells reeds in Someday Harbor: ten notes for ten gold.

hints.q: The hermit's garden? What hermit?
hints.a: Eventually Falls has a waterfall at the top of town. Its left side is only spray: walk straight up through it.

hints.q: The nest is empty.
hints.a: Watch it. Every twenty seconds or so something turns up in it for a moment. Stand on the nest and press ENTER while it's there.

hints.q: Just draw me a map.
hints.a: Up the main street to the foot of the falls, through the left edge of the falling water, and into the garden. The nest is right of the hermit; the stone beside it opens for whoever carries the egg.
